title: Stakeholder action summary & fallback options (customer-facing draft)
content:
Executive TL;DR:
We observed a partial inference degradation affecting streaming responses for a subset of tenants in eu-central-1 between 2029-11-09T22:05Z and 2029-11-10T01:40Z. The platform automatically routed most requests to fallback model variants within <2s; however, some customers experienced increased latency and trimmed streams. This draft contains short and expanded status-page templates, a concise postmortem for customer distribution, recommended customer actions, and selectable remediation options for partners who want to opt into proactive replay or credits.

Purpose of this draft:
- Provide ready-to-send statuspage and email copy in short and expanded formats.
- Offer a clear timeline and root-cause summary suitable for customer-facing postmortem.
- Give customers explicit, actionable choices (replay, request evidence, accept credit) with expected timelines.

Short status page blurb (60–140 chars):
Partial streaming degradation in eu-central-1 affecting some tenant sessions. Automatic fallbacks engaged; limited trimming observed. Full recovery completed 2029-11-10 01:40Z. More info and remediation options: [link].

Expanded status page / customer email (for subscribers and affected tenants):
Summary: Between 2029-11-09 22:05Z and 2029-11-10 01:40Z, a subset of requests routed to the eu-central-1 inference fleet returned truncated or delayed streamed responses. The platform detected degraded kernel scheduling on a small pool of GPUs which caused intermittent KV-cache eviction and partial stream truncation. Automatic routing moved traffic to compatible model variants and unaffected regions; however, some callers timed out before the fallback completed, causing truncated content.
Impact: If you use streaming responses you may have seen truncated outputs or elevated latency for requests routed through eu-central-1. Non-streaming generation and embeddings were unaffected. We estimate ~0.6% of total requests during the window were impacted, concentrated among tenants with long-lived streaming sessions.
What we did:
- Identified the affected GPU pool and throttled inbound assignments to allow cache warmup.
- Applied a hotfix to kernel selection logic to prevent aggressive cache eviction (deployed 2029-11-10 00:30Z).
- Rebalanced traffic off the impacted pool and gradually restored normal routing.
- Ran verification tests and replayed sampled requests to validate output integrity.
Customer-facing root cause (brief):
A scheduling interaction between the kernel selector and the KV cache eviction heuristic caused premature eviction under certain long-token sessions. This led to truncated streams when fallback routing did not complete before client timeouts.
Data integrity note:
We have found no evidence of data leakage or model parameter corruption. All requests are logged per our retention policy and audit trail is available on request.

Timeline (concise):
- 2029-11-09 22:05Z — First alerts: increased stream aborts in eu-central-1.
- 2029-11-09 22:12Z — Incident declared; SRE and Serving Runtime paged.
- 2029-11-09 22:30Z — Throttling and traffic rebalancing started.
- 2029-11-10 00:30Z — Kernel selection patch deployed, partial recovery observed.
- 2029-11-10 01:05Z — Gradual routing normalization.
- 2029-11-10 01:40Z — Verification completed; incident resolved.

Customer remediation options (choose one):
1) Automated replay and verification (recommended for affected tenants)
   - We will re-run impacted non-sensitive requests against recovered paths and provide a verification log of outputs and checksums. Estimated delivery: within 72 hours of opt-in.
   - No code changes required on your side. Opt-in link: [customer-replay-opt-in].
2) Manual evidence package (for compliance-heavy customers)
   - We will assemble request/response traces, timing breakdowns, and routing logs for your tenant. Delivery: within 5 business days.
3) Service credit (fast-track)
   - For customers who prefer credits instead of replay, we propose a pro-rated service credit equal to 1 day of average consumption during the incident window. Requests for credit will be processed within 7 business days after confirmation.
4) No action / acknowledgement only
   - If you saw no customer impact or do not require remediation, no action is needed.

Recommended statuspage/email templates (editable)
Subject: Incident report: Partial streaming degradation — eu-central-1 (RECOVERED)\Body (short): We experienced a partial streaming degradation in eu-central-1 on 2029-11-09. Automatic fallbacks engaged and the issue was resolved by 2029-11-10 01:40Z. If you were affected and want a replay or evidence package, please select an option here: [link].\Body (detailed): [include expanded paragraph above plus options list].

Q&A / Anticipated customer questions
Q: Were my prompts or data exposed?
A: No evidence of data exposure. Logs and audit trails show no unauthorized access; request/response items are retained per the tenant's retention settings.
Q: Why did fallback not prevent truncation for some requests?
A: Fallback routing moved traffic but some clients have short streaming timeouts; if the client timed out before the fallback completed, the client-side stream would appear truncated. We are recommending longer client-side streaming timeouts where possible as a mitigation.
Q: Will this impact my SLAs?
A: We are evaluating SLA credit eligibility case-by-case. Customers affected by truncated outputs will be eligible to request credit per the remediation options above.

Suggested technical mitigations for integrators (bullet list):
- Increase client streaming timeout to at least 20 seconds for long sessions.
- Enable the platform's streaming prefetch flag for long-lived sessions (contact SE to enable).
- If you rely on strict ordering, enable per-request sequence ids to detect truncation and automatically retry.

Post-incident engineering actions (public-facing summary):
- Permanent fix: Adjust kernel selection thresholds to respect long-session cache residency. ETA: 2029-11-20.
- Observability: Added a streaming-abort metric and tenant-focused alert rule. Deployed 2029-11-11.
- Client guidance: New best-practice doc on streaming resilience to be published 2029-11-14.

How to request remediation:
- Use the tenant admin console -> Incidents -> Request remediation, or reply to this email with your tenant id and preferred option.
- For enterprise customers, your CSM will receive a private packet with evidence and options within 24 hours.

Contacts and escalation:
- Primary CS contact: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai)
- Technical verification lead: Alejandro Ruiz (alejandro@redwood.ai)
- Escalation: cs-incident@redwood.ai (subject: INC-5123 customer escalation)

Draft notes for internal reviewers:
- Tone: keep it direct and low-jargon for customer communications; include technical appendix for enterprise recipients.
- Compensation options: credit amount above is a placeholder pending final impact calculation from Billing.
- Legal/Compliance: recommended that we add a short legal-safe sentence about liability limits before sending to regulated customers.

Appendix: sample verification checklist for replays
- Confirm request ids and timestamps match incident window.
- Run replay through the recovered routing path and record response checksums.
- Flag any non-deterministic differences for manual review.
- Provide a log with: original response size, replay response size, routing path, kernel selection tag.

End of draft.
